questions.question: What is a cost model in ServiceNow Financial Management?

options.text: A template for creating project budgets
A set of rules, methods, and metrics that define how expenses are allocated to accounts in a hierarchy
A report showing actual versus planned costs

explanation.correct: A cost model is a set of rules, methods, and metrics that tell the Financial Management application how to allocate expenses to the accounts in the hierarchy. Cost models are associated with allocations and reports, giving you control over your expense allocation.

wrongAnswers.explanation: A cost model is not a template for budgets; it defines allocation rules for expenses
Reports are separate from cost models; cost models define how allocations are calculated
Dashboards display information but cost models define allocation logic

source.excerpt: A cost model is a set of rules, methods, and metrics that tell the application how to allocate expenses to the accounts in the hierarchy.

questions.question: Which components are used by the Financial Management application to allocate expenses? (Choose THREE)

explanation.correct: The Financial Management application uses the general ledger (a list of organizational expenses), fiscal period (the time frame during which expenses were incurred), and cost models (the underlying records that define how expenses are allocated) to allocate expenses.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Change requests are part of Change Management, not Financial Management allocation
Incident records are part of Incident Management, not Financial Management allocation

source.excerpt: The Financial Management application uses these components: The general ledger, The fiscal period, The cost models, The allocation engine.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a component of a cost model in Financial Management?

explanation.correct: Resource plans are part of Resource Management, not Financial Management cost models. Cost models consist of bucket allocations, segment rollups, rollup overrides, and allocation metrics that define how expenses are allocated.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Bucket allocations are a component of cost models, defining how buckets are allocated to segments
Segment rollups define how amounts roll up from one segment to another
Allocation metrics contain additional instructions for allocating expenses based on weighted calculations

source.excerpt: To allocate expenses, the application uses the following items: Bucket allocations, Segment rollups, Rollup overrides, Allocation metrics.

questions.question: What happens when the Financial Management application processes a chargeback expense with a fixed amount method?

options.text: The fixed amount is added to the expense total
The fixed amount is processed in the opposite way, applying a credit
The chargeback is ignored by fixed amount methods
The expense is doubled to account for the chargeback

explanation.correct: The Financial Management application supports chargebacks, or negative amounts in general ledger expenses. Chargeback expenses process fixed amount methods in the opposite way. For example, a fixed amount method that allocates $50 on a $100 chargeback (shown as -100) applies a $50 credit.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Chargebacks are negative amounts, so fixed amounts are processed as credits, not additions
Fixed amount methods do process chargebacks, but in the opposite direction
Chargebacks do not double expenses; they apply credits

source.excerpt: Chargeback expenses process fixed amount methods in the opposite way of other expenses.

questions.question: Which roles can administer cost allocations through the workbench in Financial Management? (Choose TWO)

explanation.correct: Users with the financial management administrator or financial analyst role can administer cost allocations through the workbench. The workbench is the preferred method for managing allocations.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Project managers work with Project Management, not Financial Management allocations
Resource managers work with Resource Management, not Financial Management allocations

source.excerpt: Users with the financial management administrator or financial analyst role can administer cost allocations through the workbench.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about Financial Management cost model attributes is TRUE?

I. User Group association restricts which users can access the cost model.
II. Fiscal Period determines the time frame for financial modeling activities.
III. Data Source defines the staged lines source for the cost model.
IV. Cost models can only be used with a defined data source.

explanation.correct: Cost models have User Group (restricts access), Fiscal Period (sets time frame for financial modeling), and Data Source (defines staged lines source) attributes. However, you can optionally not define a data source, in which case you can create groomed lines directly or enter amounts directly into buckets.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Statement III is also true; Data Source defines the staged lines source
Statement IV is false; data source is optional
Statement IV is false; cost models can work without a defined data source

source.excerpt: Cost models have the following attributes: User Group, Fiscal Period, Data Source. Optionally, you can opt not to define a data source.
